quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale:
Section 20 already delivers the preferred position. Clause 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, extended to Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel (Affiliate is broadly defined at 1.1). Clause 20.2 adds the required misconduct limbs: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud — matching, and in the case of fraud and bodily injury exceeding, our model language. Clause 20.4 sets out standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no prejudicial settlement without consent). Clause 20.5 provides the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies for infringement claims and, helpfully, states they are in addition to (not in lieu of) the defence obligation and bars termination of unaffected Services.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow: limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorised use, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions. Vendor's IP indemnity carries no Customer-modification/combination exclusions, so we sit at the preferred rather than the fallback position, and no 3× super-cap is needed. Clause 21.3 further confirms that indemnification obligations, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP infringement are Excluded Claims and therefore sit outside the mutual liability cap in 21.1. No edit required for this rule.

quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
rationale: On re-examination the refund limb of the remedy does not hold up, so I have moved this from compliant to deviation. Section 19.4 refunds "Fees paid for it", and "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as meaning only the "Implementation Fee", which § 1.6 fixes as the one-time USD 12,000 implementation charge in the first Order Form. Read through the definitions, the refund is therefore capped at implementation money and can never return the subscription fees we pay for Hosted Services or for Deliverables — the very amounts at risk if the full-term Hosted Services conformance warranty in § 19.2 is breached. The rule requires a real remedy of repair, replacement or refund; a refund that structurally excludes the principal consideration is not one, so the defect is substantive rather than cosmetic and sits in the remedy element the playbook treats as essential. The fix is minimal and surgical: key the refund to all amounts paid for the affected item, including prepaid subscription and other charges and expressly not limited to the Implementation Fee. The re-perform/repair/replace ladder, the reasonable-period trigger and the non-exclusivity carve-out for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims are all left untouched. I also stated the Deliverable warranty period as "ninety (90) days" in numerals in § 19.2. That is a clarity conform only, not a change of term: the period already ran ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance, and expressing it in digits removes any doubt that the 90-day floor is met while keeping the drafting consistent with the rest of the Agreement. Every other element of the rule remains satisfied and needs no edit: § 19.1 gives professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel to industry standards plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications, reinforced by § 3.1; § 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conform throughout the subscription term, which meets or exceeds the 12-month software benchmark given "Services" is defined at § 1.8 to include the hosted software; § 19.3 covers Applicable Law compliance, no malicious code, no mid-term functionality diminution and open-source protection for our source code; and § 19.5 confines the disclaimer to implied warranties and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies, so no disclaimer carve-out is needed. § 21.4 preserves the caps on failure of an exclusive remedy without recasting § 19.4 as a sole remedy, and § 6 supports the warranty trigger. The residual narrowing of the malicious-code warranty to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" remains customary and not worth negotiating capital at medium severity.
